messages.text:
PR 109 is merged:

- with 2 mm and an effective 75 % of channel reduction, we should have less requirement on cables, power and cooling
- please redesign the short strip detector accordingly
- ideally this should yield less radial gap between the short and the long strip endcaps
- and it should have a positive effect on the tracker material



Here's what I need:

- a new baseline design for the short strips + cables + cooling with eventually increased radial outer coverage of the short strips
- flag if this needs a redesign of the modules

I’ll review the merged baseline and service budgets, then develop a revised short-strip design covering power, cables, cooling and endcap coverage. I’ll distinguish savings achievable with the current module footprint from changes that require a module redesign, and quantify the effect on tracker material.

The current service geometry did not shrink when 2 mm strixels were selected. A redesign is needed to realize material savings: sensor leakage, data traffic, connectors and cooling infrastructure do not all scale with channel count.

I’m using the repository’s design-evidence and validation skills, with separate tracker, interface and physics assessments. The design will state its power assumptions and check voltage drop, heat removal and routing before reducing any service envelopes.

Two constraints have emerged. The old endcap heat path is inadequate even for the reduced power assumptions, so the module’s thermal interface needs redesign. Also, an aggressive extra outer ring crowds both the service corridor and neighboring thermal pickups.

I’m evaluating a five-ring arrangement with increased outer coverage, thinner power services and improved thermal contacts. The larger sixth-ring option will remain a clearly flagged alternative if it needs further module or routing changes.

A feasible coverage candidate now has five short-strip rings extending to about **704 mm**, up from **672 mm**, without moving the long strips. That reduces the physical active radial gap from roughly **115 mm to 83 mm**.

The narrower service trunk also requires a wider barrel collector connection; reducing the trunk alone would create a bottleneck. I’m including that connection and the added sensors in the power, cooling and material budgets.

The redesign can extend the short-strip active radius from **672.5 to 703.9 mm** while keeping the long strips fixed. It does require module changes: fewer readout channels alone do not provide an adequate thermal path.

I’m allowing for connectors and protection devices in the power budget. That favors 10 mm² supply and return conductors; the proposed 8 mm cable package still needs supplier qualification. Cooling tube diameters remain unchanged until hydraulic checks justify a reduction.

The current model predicts a material saving even after adding the larger endcaps, thicker heat spreaders, direct thermal inserts and a service-material reserve. The main saving comes from power cabling: **1,584 → 1,008 feeds**, with the fibre allocation retained.

Cooling is more constrained. Each endcap petal needs two circuits, so the design adds branches and manifolds. I’m reporting this as a conditional cable and material saving; it does not imply a 75% reduction in cooling hardware.
Go ahead and do the module redesign to advance the coverage to 703 mm

I’ll carry the module redesign into an isolated geometry prototype and check coverage to 703 mm. That includes the thermal inserts, spreader, electronics placement, power flex and revised endcap mounts. I’ll verify the full azimuthal coverage, since the outermost sensor corner alone does not establish coverage at every angle.

I’m using the ACTS/Spack skill to verify the native geometry tools before building the prototype. Its preflight found changed setup and lockfile fingerprints, so the older environment record is no longer sufficient; I’ll check the installed runtime directly.

I’m also extending the thermal model into an explicit pipe-contact geometry. That may require a longer insert and a larger material allowance than the initial thermal sketch.

The updated layout covers the sampled full azimuth through **703 mm**, with an outermost active corner at **704.9 mm**. The gap to long-strip silicon becomes **82.3 mm**.

I’ve enlarged the thermal-insert allowance to include a saddle around the cooling pipe. This reduces the conservative material-saving estimate to about **135 kg**, with no credit for cable-insulation or ASIC mass savings. The native prototype will now check the module windows, saddles, mounts and neighboring modules for overlaps.

The explicit geometry exposed a flaw in the inherited cooling layout: some edge modules had thermal lands that missed the tube. I’m correcting it with a central thermal saddle and tighter hairpin routing that reaches every module.

The revised source check finds contact for all 33 modules per petal. Native construction is running next to verify the solid contacts and check overlaps, including neighboring petals.

The first native check found that an 18 mm saddle touched neighboring sensor guards. I’ve narrowed it to **16 × 60 mm**, preserving the silicon and guards; the contact check still reaches every module.

The final geometry check is now running at a fixed revision. The updated thermal screen gives **−22.2 °C** at the adverse load with −35 °C coolant, conditional on the specified contact properties. The conservative material estimate is now about **115 kg saved**, including the redesigned inserts and extra sensors.

The redesigned endcap prototype passes native construction: **792 sensors, zero ROOT overlaps at 10⁻⁵ mm**, correct 75 µm × 2 mm cell indexing, and all **7,200 contact/window probes** passing.

A separate source check found no barrel insert clashes with neighboring modules or services. I’m completing the final review and repeatable validation recipe; ASIC feasibility and thermal/hydraulic qualification remain open.

The final review found that the thermal estimate also needs explicit allowances for the ASIC bond and the sensor’s leakage-heat path. Including those gives an adverse estimate of **−20.33 °C**, leaving only about **0.33 °C** to the −20 °C target.

The mechanical geometry has passed. I’m recording the tighter thermal budget as a requirement to demonstrate, then refreshing the evidence so the temperature result and geometry provenance agree.

The design, plots and reproduction scripts are complete. I’m closing the validation records and checking the final file set. It contains source code, plots and compact summaries; generated XML, ROOT files and build outputs remain local.

The main remaining constraint is thermal qualification: the complete adverse budget has only a **0.33 K margin**. Full-tracker material and reconstruction studies are still needed for this changed geometry.

The module redesign is complete as a validated prototype. The proposed layout reaches the **703 mm sampled coverage target** and reduces the active radial gap to **82.3 mm**. The final native check passes with zero overlaps, and all 20 portable tests pass.

I’ve saved the design, five figure sets, compact evidence and reproduction scripts. The thermal margin, cable-package feasibility and remaining full-tracker checks are documented.

Implemented the **703 mm endcap module prototype**.

| Quantity | New design |
|---|---:|
| Sampled radial coverage | **703 mm** |
| Gap to long-strip silicon | **114.8 → 82.3 mm** |
| Sensors per disc | **360 → 396** |
| Power bundles, both ends | **1,584 → 1,008** |
| Conservative scoped material saving | **≈115 kg** |

The module retains the sensor outline and adds a **16 × 60 mm thermal saddle**, revised cooling routes, spreader, electronics arrangement and mounts.

Validation passed: **792 sensors, zero native overlaps, 7,200 probes and 20 tests**.

The thermal margin is only **0.33 K** under the stated assumptions. ASIC/cable feasibility, native barrel construction and full-tracker material scans remain pending.

[Design, plots and reproduction recipes]([redacted] No run payloads committed.
